newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Gulf jet fuel headed west as Asia demand seen weak.
newsitem.headline: Gulf jet fuel headed west as Asia demand seen weak.

text.p: Saudi Arabian jet fuel, faced with weak Asian demand, was sold for export to Northwest Europe (NWE) and Africa last week, traders said on Monday.

Traders said they expected the Saudi jet to continue being attractive for export to these markets as the big Asian buyers, India and Japan, were not buying large amounts of jet fuel for November arrivals.
They added that stocks of unsold jet fuel in independent storage facilities in Guam, Singapore and the Gulf were high.
Japan was well stocked for the coming winter and has yet to buy incremental spot barrels for arrival in November and it was only making limited enquiries for December arrival cargoes, traders said.
India bought one 45,000 tonne superior kerosene cargo for arrival in November in a monthly purchase tender, which closed last last week, below market expectations of two or three cargoes.
Traders had said India needed to buy at least five cargoes in order to tighten what is fundamentally a weak Asian market.

Jet fuel prices in Singapore were hovering around $30.00 per tonne, despite big increases to gas oil prices. As a result the jet fuel/gas oil swap spread for October crunched from $2.15 in late September to about 90 cents now.
Last week, three 30,000-tonne cargoes were sold free-on-board (fob) Red Sea at between flat-to-five cent premium over spot Middle East quotes, traders said.
A 30,000-tonne cargo, acquired by a major, is heading to East Africa, traders said. Another has been acquired by a trader but its destination has not been decided, they said.

But one cargo, bought by another major, is for export to NWE where prices are pegged at about $30 per tonne above the International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) gas oil futures price in London, traders said.
They said they believed this was the first Red Sea-sourced cargo sold to NWE on a prompt basis.
Based on Friday's October gas oil close on the IPE of $245.50 per tonne, the price of jet fuel in Rotterdam was assessed at about $273.00 per tonne fob.
At this price, it is about $50 per tonne above the prevailing spot quotes in the Gulf which are assessed at about $28.50 per barrel ($224.50) on a free-on-board basis.
Traders said it was not easy to move jet fuel from the Middle East to NWE because a six-percent European import levy added to costs.
Traders said a contango in near-term Gulf prices was allowing the arbitrage into Europe to work. Further out prices were too narrow compared with European values, they said.
The contango costs for cargoes loading out of the Gulf were at about 80 cents per barrel per month, traders said.

Jet fuel cargoes were still available for loading in end October or early November from various Gulf countries, including Saudi Arabia and Kuwait, at about flat to a slight premium to Mideast quotes, traders said.
